## trove-workflow

> Workflow methodology skills and session bootstrap

| Skill | What it does | Triggers | Paths |
|-------|--------------|----------|-------|
| **trove-arena** | Spawn N parallel candidate attempts at one hard, novel artifact, pick the strongest base, graft the best ideas from the losers into it, then verify. A heavyweight technique — most work routes to trove-architect instead. Use only for a genuinely novel, hard-to-reverse design decision with no precedent. | `throw it in the arena`, `try several approaches in parallel`, `competing prototypes` | — |
| **trove-autoplan** | Front-door planning workflow. Take an idea and produce implementation-ready output by composing the Trove product skills (spec → user stories → release-note preview). Defers all detail to the leaf skills it calls. | `autoplan`, `turn this idea into a plan`, `draft an implementation plan`, `end-to-end planning` | — |
| **trove-brainstorm** | Feature and design brainstorming gate. Use before implementing a new feature, UI, refactor, or product change when no approved design exists. | `let's build`, `add a feature`, `design this`, `refactor this flow`, `brainstorm` | — |
| **trove-debug** | Systematic debugging workflow. Use for bug reports, failing tests, broken behavior, red CI, regressions, or unexplained production symptoms. | `bug report`, `test failure`, `this is broken`, `red ci`, `debug` | — |
| **trove-dispatch** | Parallel-agent dispatch workflow. Use when a request contains multiple independent tasks that can be safely delegated. | `parallel agents`, `dispatch tasks`, `multiple independent tasks`, `delegate this` | — |
| **trove-execute-plan** | Execute an approved implementation plan one checkpoint at a time with verification before advancing. | `execute the plan`, `implement this plan`, `go checkpoint by checkpoint`, `continue the plan` | — |
| **trove-plan** | Implementation planning workflow. Use after brainstorm approval or for multi-step work that needs verifiable checkpoints. | `write a plan`, `implementation plan`, `break this down`, `multi-step change` | — |
| **trove-principle-data-shape** | Foundational Thinking — get the data shape right before writing logic. Choose core types and structures first; a late data-structure change is a rewrite, early it is a one-line diff. Use before writing logic, choosing core types, or sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work. | `what's the data shape`, `model this first`, `foundational thinking` | — |
| **trove-principle-encode-in-structure** | Encode Lessons in Structure — when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, encode it as a lint, rubric, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more prose. The repeated instruction is the symptom. Use when a correction recurs, or when tempted to add another "remember to…" line. | `encode this as a check`, `stop repeating this instruction`, `make this structural` | — |
| **trove-principle-idempotency** | Make Operations Idempotent — design commands, lifecycle steps, and processing loops to converge to the same end state regardless of how many times they run or where they start from. Use when designing operations that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries (jobs, deploys, lifecycle steps, queues). | `make this idempotent`, `safe to retry`, `converge to the same state` | — |
| **trove-principle-laziness** | Laziness Protocol — aim for the most result with the least code and complexity; bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem. Use when refactoring, weighing diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. | `is this over-engineered`, `simplest change`, `laziness protocol` | — |
| **trove-principle-migrate-then-delete** | Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs — when introducing a new internal API while old callers exist, migrate every caller and delete the old API in the same refactor wave instead of leaving a compatibility layer. Use when replacing an internal API, function, or module that has no external dependents. | `migrate callers`, `remove the legacy api`, `no compatibility shim` | — |
| **trove-principle-type-discipline** | Type System Discipline — treat the type checker as a proof assistant: make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, don't lie to the compiler. Applies to any statically typed language. Use when designing types or a signature in TypeScript, Python (hints/Pydantic), Swift, or similar. | `design these types`, `make illegal states unrepresentable`, `type system discipline` | — |
| **trove-receive-review** | Review-feedback handling workflow. Use when the user provides PR comments, code review feedback, or requested changes. | `address review`, `pr comments`, `code review feedback`, `requested changes` | — |
| **trove-refactor** | Behavior-preserving change to structure: rename, extract, inline, dedupe, move, or migrate an internal API. Pin behavior first, migrate callers and delete the legacy API in one wave, prove behavior unchanged on the real artifact. Use for refactors and internal-API migrations. | `refactor this`, `migrate callers`, `extract this`, `delete the legacy api` | — |
| **trove-reflect** | Mine the current session for durable learnings and route each into a concrete edit — a skill change or a learnings entry — never auto-applied. Use when the user says "reflect", or after a session that surfaced a recurring correction or a non-obvious project quirk. | `reflect on this session`, `what did we learn`, `capture learnings` | — |
| **trove-ship** | Front-door ship workflow. Prepare a change for landing by composing the review and commit skills, surfacing a final Decision Gate before any destructive action. Thin orchestrator — defers detail to leaf skills. | `ship this change`, `prepare to land`, `get this PR-ready`, `ship workflow` | — |
| **trove-show-work** | Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: an append-only TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result).
